words.gloss: by the excellence of their intellect

literal: Those of common beauty's lowly pleasure will not embrace, by the excellence of their intellect, those of glorious wisdom.
translation: Those who possess glorious wisdom, arising from an excellent intellect, will not embrace the lowly pleasure offered by women of public beauty.
modern: இயற்கையான அறிவு நுட்பத்தால் சிறந்த அறிவைப் பெற்றவர்கள், பொதுவான அழகை விற்கும் மகளிரின் இழிவான இன்பத்தைப் பொருந்த மாட்டார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the company of public women, referred to here as 'potunalamttār' (those whose beauty is common or public). The poet explains that those who possess 'māṇṭa aṟiviṉavar' (glorious wisdom) which is sharpened by 'matinalam' (excellence of intellect) will never seek 'punnalam' (lowly or worthless pleasure). The word 'punnalam' combines 'pul' (lowly/worthless) and 'nalam' (pleasure/benefit) to describe the fleeting, commercial nature of such relationships. True wisdom guides a person to recognize the emptiness of such pursuits and avoid them entirely.
